title: Freelancing in California with a saxophone section
summary: On the West Coast he, Ralph Spangler and Tim Lanfier moved from local band to band as a section; he recalls Earl Burnett, Gus Arnheim and Phil Harris.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: And on the West Coast, according to Chilton, you were free lancing, and then you moved back to New York. With whom on the West Coast?

Well, actually, this saxophone player, a guy by the name of Ralph Spangler, he was there with me, and we kind of joined up with another guy by the name of Tim Lanfier, who was also a saxophone player, and we had like a saxophone section. And I can't tell you the names of anybody we played with there because we were never with anybody that long, because we were totally unruly and we would join the band as a section and we would leave as a section. If anybody said boo to one of us all three of us would leave. And we

played around with, oh, just the local bands there. I couldn't tell you the name of one of them, at that time in California. I think about the only bands that anybody had ever heard of were the Burnett Band, Earl Burnett, and he was at the Biltmore, and then there was the Gus Arnheim Orchestra. Then maybe up in San Francisco there was a band up there. I can't think of his name at the moment, but Phil Harris, he didn't even -- he was still the Loughner Lofner Harris Orchestra. Phil played drums and sat down. In fact nobody stood up. They just -- he was just in the front row with the drums.
I -- I can't remember the name of the place. It was some ballroom. I can see it. It was down there on Pershing Square. It was up on the second floor.

No, no. It was only a two story building. It was on the same square as the Biltmore, but I can't remember the name of the ballroom. I don't know if it's still there or not. I'm sure it isn't as a ballroom, but --
